dish.title: Smoky Pumpkin and Pinto Bean Chili

Finished with lime and topped with diced avocado, radish, cilantro, and crushed corn tortilla chips. Plant-based; no cheese, no sour cream.

recipe_version.title: Smoky Pumpkin and Pinto Bean Chili
recipe_version.description: A thick, brick-red pinto bean chili built on smoked paprika, chili powder, and fire-roasted tomatoes, with canned pumpkin melted in for body and a gentle sweetness. Finished with lime and topped with diced avocado, radish, cilantro, and crushed corn tortilla chips. Plant-based; no cheese, no sour cream.

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil
ingredients.note: for softening the onion and pepper

ingredients.name: chili powder
ingredients.note: Store-bought spice blend. HARD CONTRACT: plain blend whose label lists only ground chiles, spices, salt, garlic (and an anti-caking agent). No added flour, no 'chili seasoning mix' packets.

ingredients.name: ground chipotle chile
ingredients.note: pure ground chipotle (single spice), not chipotles in adobo. Adds smoky heat; use 1/4 tsp for mild.

ingredients.name: pumpkin puree
ingredients.note: 1 (15-oz) can. HARD CONTRACT: 100% pure pumpkin, NOT pumpkin pie filling (which is sweetened and spiced).

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: HARD CONTRACT: vegetable broth. Not chicken, beef, or bone broth. Choose a carton with no milk listed.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1/2 tsp with the onion and pepper, 1 tsp with the liquids; adjust at the end

ingredients.name: avocados
ingredients.note: topping; also the creamy element in place of sour cream
ingredients.preparation: halved, pitted, and diced just before serving

ingredients.name: radishes
ingredients.preparation: trimmed and thinly sliced into coins

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.preparation: leaves and tender stems, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: corn tortilla chips
ingredients.note: topping. HARD CONTRACT: plain corn tortilla chips whose label lists only corn (masa/lime), oil, and salt, fried in corn, sunflower, safflower, or canola oil. Not peanut oil, not cheese- or ranch-flavored, no wheat.

steps.title: Prep the vegetables, spices, and toppings
steps.body: Dice the onion and the red bell pepper (1/2-inch). Mince the garlic. In a small bowl combine the 2 tbsp chili powder, 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp ground chipotle, and 1 tsp oregano. Measure the 2 tbsp tomato paste. Open the pumpkin and tomatoes; drain and rinse the pinto beans. For the toppings: thinly slice the radishes, chop the cilantro, juice 1 lime (about 2 tbsp) and cut the other into wedges, and lightly crush the tortilla chips in their bag. Leave the avocados whole for now. Confirm the contracts: vegetable broth, 100% pure pumpkin, plain corn chips. About 12 minutes.

steps.title: Soften the onion and pepper
steps.body: Heat the 2 tbsp olive oil in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, and 1/2 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and the onion edges turn golden, 6 to 7 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant. About 8 minutes.

steps.title: Bloom the spices and tomato paste
steps.body: Add the spice mix and the tomato paste. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the paste darkens to brick red and the spices smell toasty. Lower the heat if anything starts to scorch. About 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the chili
steps.body: Add the pumpkin puree, the fire-roasted tomatoes with their juices, the pinto beans, the 2 cups vegetable broth, and the remaining 1 tsp kosher salt. Stir well, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom. Raise the heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer, about 5 minutes. Reduce to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until thick enough to mound on a spoon. In the last 5 minutes, press about 1 cup of the beans against the side of the pot with the spoon and stir them back in to thicken. While it simmers, halve, pit, and dice the avocados (this overlaps the simmer and adds no time). About 20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with lime and top
steps.body: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and add salt if needed. Ladle into wide bowls. Top each with diced avocado, radish coins, cilantro, and a handful of crushed tortilla chips; serve lime wedges alongside. No cheese, no sour cream. About 3 minutes. kitchen_tested is false.

components.name: avocado, radish, cilantro, and tortilla-chip toppings
components.contract: Assembled from raw/whole ingredients; tortilla chips are store-bought with a plain-corn, non-peanut-oil contract.

equipment: 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven or heavy pot
recipe_version.time_clock: Prep 12 (all dicing, spice mix, toppings except avocado). Cook 33 = 8 soften + 2 bloom + 20 (5 return to simmer + 15 uncovered simmer) + 3 finish. Avocado dicing overlaps the simmer. Stovetop only; no oven, so no preheat.
recipe_version.heat: Stovetop only. Medium to soften the onion and pepper; medium-high to return to a simmer; medium-low uncovered simmer. No oven.
recipe_version.doneness: Chili thick enough to mound on a spoon; beans tender and some crushed into the base; pumpkin fully melted into a brick-red, glossy chili; no raw spice taste. kitchen_tested is false.

dietary_eligibility.nut_policy_note: No peanuts, tree nuts, or cashews. Tortilla chips are contracted not to be fried in peanut oil. Avocado is a fruit, not a nut.
dietary_eligibility.hh001_reason: Plant-based chili. No dairy (no cheese, no sour cream; avocado is the creamy topping), no shellfish, no meat, no poultry, no nuts. Vegetable broth, 100% pure pumpkin, and plain corn tortilla chips (non-peanut oil) are hard shopping contracts, not 'if' claims.

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Unconditional dairy_free, vegetarian, and plant_based. Every ingredient is plant-derived. Vegetable broth (never chicken/beef/bone broth) and plain corn chips are hard contracts. No cheese or sour cream garnish anywhere in the recipe.
allergen_notes: No allergen tokens: no egg, milk, peanut, tree_nut, soy, wheat, sesame, shellfish, finfish, meat, or poultry in the written ingredients.
Tortilla chips are contracted as plain corn chips (corn, oil, salt) fried in a non-peanut oil, so no wheat or peanut token.
Chili powder is contracted as a plain spice blend with no added flour.
The allergen list is an explicit empty list, not an omission.
recipe_version.hh001_reason: Plant-based chili. No dairy (no cheese, no sour cream; avocado is the creamy topping), no shellfish, no meat, no poultry, no nuts. Vegetable broth, 100% pure pumpkin, and plain corn tortilla chips (non-peanut oil) are hard shopping contracts, not 'if' claims.

scaling_notes.1: Quarter everything; use a 2-quart saucepan. Use about 1/4 of the pumpkin can (about 1/2 cup) and refrigerate the rest. The smaller volume thickens faster: simmer about 10 minutes.
scaling_notes.2: Halve everything in a 3-quart saucepan; 1 can of beans; about half the pumpkin can. Simmer about 12 minutes.

coverage_contribution: Opens the chili format (0 in the 50-meal base; deferred twice). October pumpkin; pinto beans stay out of the black-bean Mexican cluster. The only new legume-led HH001 meal this wave, and HH001's first chili.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Smoky Lentil Sweet Potato Stew: both smoky plant pots, but that is a lentil-sweet-potato stew; this is a bean chili with chili-powder/cumin/oregano spicing, pumpkin body, and fresh crunchy toppings. Compared with Chipotle Lime Black Bean Bowls, Black Bean Quesadillas, and Crispy Chipotle Tofu Tacos: different bean (pinto), different format (pot chili vs bowl/handheld), no rice. Compared with White Bean Kale Soup: brothy Italian-leaning soup vs thick spiced chili. Deliberately not turkey chili and not a black-bean chili. Not a live-catalog duplicate.
